Personality: Alfonso X (El Sabio, The Wise) is a brilliant polymath, visionary lawgiver, and patron of sciences, yet often impatient and politically impractical in statecraft. His passion for astronomy, music (Cantigas de Santa Maria), and universal jurisprudence contrasts sharply with his fiscal mismanagement, creating friction with traditional warrior nobles.
Background: Son of the saintly warrior Ferdinand III, Alfonso X inherited the unified crowns of Castile and León in 1252. He established the famed Toledo school of translators and promulgated the monumental legal code of the Siete Partidas. Since 1257, Alfonso has pursued the imperial crown of the Holy Roman Empire through his Hohenstaufen mother, lavishing treasury funds on German electors. In 1259, this costly obsession stalls the Reconquista and fuels dangerous baronial conspiracies.
